headline: Public Law 115-245 provides fiscal year 2019 funding for the Defense Department, Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education, and keeps other agencies funded through December 7, 2018 so a partial shutdown is avoided.
what_it_does: The law is a combined spending bill with four parts. Division A funds Department of Defense military activities, Division B funds the Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education along with several related agencies, and Division C is a continuing resolution that keeps other agencies running at fiscal 2018 levels through December 7, 2018 or until their full funding bills are enacted. It also extends several programs that were set to expire at the end of fiscal 2018, and it includes many rules on how the money may and may not be spent.

who_it_affects.group: Active-duty and reserve members of the military and National Guard
who_it_affects.how: They receive pay and benefits funded under the Defense appropriations division, which sets their FY2019 personnel dollars.

who_it_affects.group: Federal Medicaid, CHIP, and Medicare-related program participants
who_it_affects.how: Entitlement programs such as Medicaid and the Children's Health Insurance Program are funded through this law, and CHIP state allotments that remain unobligated as of September 25, 2019 are rescinded.

who_it_affects.group: Current and prospective college students and student loan borrowers
who_it_affects.how: The law includes Pell grant rescissions, lets borrowers in cancer treatment defer student loan payments, and extends account maintenance fee authority for guaranty agencies through 2019.
Pay caps, travel rules, and restrictions on contracts apply, including a bar on contracts over $1 million with companies that have not resolved certain civil rights claims.

who_it_affects.group: Federal employees and contractors working on Public Service Loan Forgiveness
who_it_affects.how: Additional funds are provided for loan cancellations under the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program, with added outreach to borrowers.

who_it_affects.group: Unaccompanied alien children in federal custody
who_it_affects.how: HHS must submit a reunification plan to Congress by November 15, 2018, and may accept private donations for their care.
Continuing resolution provisions accelerate Commodity Credit Corporation reimbursements for farm program losses and fund rural water and waste disposal loans.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted September 28, 2018; the continuing resolution funds agencies through December 7, 2018 or until the applicable full appropriations bill is enacted, and fiscal 2019 begins October 1, 2018.
